title: Kamasau language and pronunciation
text: October 14, 2024 - Kamasau is a member of the Marienberg branch of the Torricelli language family. It is spoken by about 900 people in the Turubu Rural LLG in East Sepik Province in the northwest of Papua New Guinea. In particular, it is spoken in the villages of Wandomi, Wobu, Kenyari, Kamasau, Tring and Wau.

title: Kamasau Language (KMS) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map, Endangered Level & Official Use | Ethnologue Free
text: Kamasau is an endangered indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Torricelli language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools.
